In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the coordination chemistry of anticancer drugs with iron(iii), a metal ion that is present in high concentrations in human serum.
the development of new anticancer agents, the molecular pharmacology of which is based on the coordination chemistry of iron(iii).
the molecular basis for the iron(iii) binding and the resulting redox properties of the anticancer anthracycline doxorubicin, and the quinolone anticancer vosaroxin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both vosaroxin and doxorubicin form strong iron complexes in vitro and the iron complexes of both molecules have been isolated and fully characterized in this work.
both vosaroxin and doxorubicin bind iron with similar strength and that both molecules form tris-complexes, but at physiological pH the vosaroxin complex is the dominant species.
vosaroxin has a higher affinity for iron(iii) than doxorubicin, and the Fe(iii):vosaroxin complex is more stable than the Fe(iii)-dox complex at physiological pH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fe(iii):vosaroxin system is the most stable of all the systems investigated.

the Fe(iii) binding constants of vosaroxacino and dox are comparable, however the stability of the vosaroxin complexes are greater at physiological pH and the Fe(iii)-bound vosaroxino is more stable than the Fe(iii):doxo complex.
the iron-binding properties of vosaroxino are comparable to the anthradycline anticancer agents and that vosaroxin has a greater potential to form stable iron(iii)-complexes than the anthracyclins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the iron(iii) complex with the quinolone vosaroxin is a stable species in the presence of physiological iron(iii) concentrations, whereas doxorubicin binds iron(iii) less strongly and forms a mixture of species at physiological pH.
vosaroxin is more iron(iii)-coordinated than doxorubicin, and this property could be a significant contributor to its cardiovascular safety.
the iron(iii) complex of vosaroxine may be a useful model to study the mechanism of action of the anticancer quinoline derivatives.
